evaluation_context.goal: Produce an excellent, source-faithful learner session while preserving all deterministic correctness, identity, and sequence constraints.
evaluation_context.source_fidelity_goal: Independently verify the hard-gated edited challenger against the supplied source material. Reject unsupported facts, answers, explanations, feedback, or terminology changes; do not edit the artifact.

criteria.factual_fidelity: Every claim and answer is faithful to the supplied source.
criteria.answer_unambiguity: Each item has one defensible answer under its instructions.
criteria.distractor_plausibility: Distractors are credible without becoming defensible answers.

criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.

criteria.feedback_usefulness: Feedback explains the governing concept and next step.

sources.input_id: 7. Get started with AI in Azure.md
sources.location: sources/7. Get started with AI in Azure.md

evidence.statement: Most claims and keyed answers directly match the supplied source, including tenant contents, resource settings, inference, scaling, Foundry IQ, and REST behavior.
The speech item uses “speech AI,” while the source names the capability as speech and the service as Azure Speech; this is broadly aligned but less source-exact.
Most items have one defensible keyed answer, but two fill-in items accept answers that duplicate wording already present in the stem.
Distractors generally represent credible category confusions, such as resource versus Playground versus client, or training data versus inference input versus application state.

Wrong choices are commonly labeled with realistic misconceptions and paired with corrective distinctions, including storage versus compute, Key Vault versus code, and agent orchestration versus tools.

The ordered session jumps between unrelated domains and postpones foundational AI terminology until item 21, after tenant, Foundry, security, data, and endpoint concepts; related concepts are also separated widely.
Multiple-choice, true/false, fill-in, and sentence-arrangement mechanics recur throughout the session without a prolonged run of one mechanic.
Prompt wording varies across scenarios and question forms, but arrangement prompts repeatedly use near-equivalent formulas such as “Put the pieces,” “Arrange,” and “Reconstruct.”
Several scenarios resemble credible operational decisions, including preserving tutoring state, selecting managed hosting, choosing global data storage, and matching tools to clinical modalities.
Some scenarios are mechanically constructed and mix service categories with capabilities, especially the storage-options item.
Incorrect-choice rationales often explain the governing distinction and better fit, but several correct explanations provide only “Correct,” offering no concept reminder or next step.
The checkpoint includes a useful mix of remembering, understanding, applying, and higher-rung scenarios, but advanced items are interleaved with basic recall rather than scaffolded.
Core Azure and Foundry terms are used consistently, but “speech AI” is not the source's exact label, and App Service naming varies between “App Services” and “Azure App Service.”

The artifact covers the source broadly and offers varied mechanics and useful misconception feedback, but the exact sequence lacks conceptual flow and contains two deterministic fill-in acceptance defects.

critical_defects.summary: The fill-in item accepts “intelligent tutoring system” after the stem already says “an intelligent,” producing the malformed sentence “an intelligent intelligent tutoring system.”

evidence.statement: The stem is “is an intelligent ___,” while accepted_answers includes both “tutoring system” and “intelligent tutoring system.”

critical_defects.summary: The fill-in item accepts “Azure App Service” after the stem already says “Azure,” producing the malformed phrase “Azure Azure App Service.”

evidence.statement: The stem is “Azure ___ hosts web apps,” while accepted_answers includes both “App Service” and “Azure App Service.”

largest_gap.summary: The exact ordered session does not build from foundations to applications coherently; it repeatedly switches domains and introduces basic AI concepts after advanced Azure and Foundry topics.

evidence.statement: The session begins with tenant structure and Ask AI, moves through Foundry, security, storage, and endpoints, then reaches the foundational definition of artificial intelligence at item 21 and continues alternating unrelated concepts.

largest_gap.repair_instruction: Reorder the existing items into conceptual bands: AI fundamentals and applications; Azure cloud service categories; tenant, subscription, resource group, resource, and portal; security, hosting, scaling, and storage; Foundry resource, project, models, agents, tools, and knowledge; then client workflow, endpoints, and REST. Preserve each item payload and deterministic answer.

result.concise_summary: Broadly source-faithful and mechanically varied, but the sequence has weak conceptual progression, feedback is often too terse, and two fill-in items accept malformed duplicated answers. Confidence is reduced because no approved references were supplied.

history.stop_evidence: Critic requested human review or confidence was below threshold.
